:::{#rem-flexibility}
#### Polynomial degree orders flexibility

Least-squares polynomial fits are ordered by degree:
a polynomial of degree $d$ is also a polynomial of degree $d + 1$
whose coefficient of $x^{d + 1}$ is zero,
so the fit of degree $d + 1$ is [at least as flexible](#def-flexibility)
as the fit of degree $d$.
The four fits of @exr-overfitting are ordered this way.
Procedures whose candidate sets are not nested
can be compared by other measures of flexibility,
such as the effective number of parameters
[@hastie2009elements, sec. 7.6].

:::
